verified_metadata.title: Grad-CAM: Visual Explanations from Deep Networks via Gradient-Based Localization
verified_metadata.venue: 2017 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)

metadata_sources.supports: Exact author order, title, ICCV 2017 and pages 618–626.
IEEE-deposited DOI metadata confirms DOI, author order and pagination.

artifact.version_note: Official CVF ICCV 2017 accepted version, pages 618–626; not the later IJCV extension.

contexts.evidence: Section 3 introduces gradient-weighted class activation mapping as a CAM generalization.
Sections 2–3 place Grad-CAM among class-activation mapping methods and derive its gradient-weighted activation map.
Section 3, Eq. (1), pools class-score gradients spatially. Its architectural generality is for CNN-based models with a spatial convolutional layer, not arbitrary architectures.
contexts.proposed_replacement: Grad-CAM~\parencite{Selvaraju2017} generalizes it to CNN-based architectures without requiring a global-average-pooling head by weighting each channel with the spatially pooled gradient of the class logit

contexts.evidence: Section 3 defines Grad-CAM at a convolutional layer and upsamples its coarse localization map. The thesis’s selected block is its experimental choice.
Sections 4 and 7.1 evaluate bounding-box localization and inside/outside activation ratios; they do not establish the attributed criticism of box-based metrics.
contexts.proposed_replacement: This avoids awarding foreground credit to background pixels inside an object's bounding box; pixel masks reward only mass on the actual foreground object.

notes: Duplicate identity of Selvaraju2017_existing; both point to the same ICCV 2017 paper.

verified_metadata.title: Towards robust explanations for deep neural networks

metadata_sources.supports: Publisher record verifies complete authors, title, journal volume 121, January 2022, article number and DOI.
Official preprint identity and ordered authors.

artifact.version_note: Matching arXiv:2012.10425v1 (18 December 2020), read in full relevant sections. Journal metadata is Pattern Recognition 121 (January 2022), article 108194; publication text may differ from this preprint.

contexts.evidence: Sections 2–3.3 bound gradient changes through Hessian norms and propose smoother Softplus activations; Section 4.3 trains such networks.
Sections 3.3 and 4.3 justify and test Softplus training as a defense against explanation manipulation.
Section 3.3 proposes Softplus smoothing. Its connection to the thesis’s entropy regularization is the thesis’s own result, not attributed to this paper.

Theorem 1 and §3.3 bound Hessians using weight norms and bounded activation derivatives. The ReLU limit makes this bound diverge; it does not prove every ReLU network has an unbounded Hessian. Appendix B treats distributional derivatives.
contexts.proposed_replacement: Their argument bounds the Frobenius norm of the network Hessian in terms of the weight norms and activation derivatives: the bound diverges in the ReLU limit, whereas $|\mathrm{sp}_\theta''(z)|\le 1/(4\theta)$ gives a finite uniform bound for fixed weights, and the gradient theorem then bounds changes in the gradient explanation under input perturbations.

notes: The key ending 2020 names the preprint year; the existing bibliography correctly uses the 2022 journal year.

verified_metadata.title: LayerCAM: Exploring Hierarchical Class Activation Maps for Localization

metadata_sources.supports: Author project page verifies paper identity and links the complete manuscript.
IEEE-deposited metadata verifies ordered authors, DOI, TIP 30 (2021), pages 5875–5888.

artifact.version_note: Author-hosted 14-page manuscript, linked from the author’s project page. Its template header says August 2015; this is a stale LaTeX template header, not the publication year. Published in IEEE TIP 30 (2021), 5875–5888.

contexts.evidence: Introduction and §II describe LayerCAM as a class activation mapping method.

Section II.B, Eqs. (6)–(8), pp.5–6, clips each gradient to its positive part before activation weighting. The displayed thesis formula omits that inner ReLU. Zero post-ReLU activation does not imply zero derivative with respect to that activation.
contexts.proposed_replacement: \text{LayerCAM}^{(l)} = \relu\Bigl(\sum_c \relu\!\Bigl(\frac{\partial y}{\partial \actl{l}_c}\Bigr)\odot\actl{l}_c\Bigr). Replace the final clause with: inactive neurons contribute no activation-weighted term, and the positive-gradient weighting discards negative gradient evidence.

contexts.evidence: Section II.B gives per-location positive-gradient weighting. Selecting the last convolutional block is compatible with the method; it does not exploit its optional multilevel fusion.

notes: IEEE Xplore browser access was blocked by a JavaScript challenge; author manuscript and publisher-deposited DOI metadata agree.

verified_metadata.title: From attribution maps to human-understandable explanations through Concept Relevance Propagation

metadata_sources.supports: Publisher record and PDF verify full ordered author list, exact title, volume 5, issue 9, pages and DOI.

artifact.version_note: Published open-access article, Nature Machine Intelligence 5, 1006–1019, September 2023.

contexts.evidence: Methods, p.1015, explicitly extends LRP through masked relevance propagation. This 2023 paper precedes AttnLRP (2024) and is not an extension of that transformer method.
contexts.proposed_replacement: AttnLRP \parencite{Achtibat2024AttnLRP} systematized this into dedicated rules for the bilinear products and non-linearities, scaling to \acp{llm}. Related LRP extensions provide concept-level \parencite{Achtibat2023CRP} and sign-aware \parencite{vukadin2024abslrp} explanations.

contexts.evidence: Methods, p.1015, Eqs. (7)–(9), select concepts by masking relevance messages without division by a concept marginal. This supports the distinction from a conditional probability; the NRM embedding is attributed to Xiong separately.

verified_metadata.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 32

metadata_sources.supports: Official proceedings title, authors, venue and year.
Published paper confirms exact author spelling and order, including Andreas Köpf and Zach DeVito.
Official Torchvision documentation independently supports availability of VGG-16, ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16 ImageNet-1K checkpoint families; this is not covered by the 2019 paper.

artifact.version_note: Official NeurIPS 2019 proceedings PDF, 12 pages; title and all 21 authors inspected.

contexts.evidence: Sections 3–5 describe PyTorch programming, tensor execution and automatic differentiation. They do not construct the thesis split-pair converter; the citation currently follows the converter claim, obscuring the software-only attribution.
contexts.proposed_replacement: a converter implemented in PyTorch~\parencite{Paszke2019PyTorch} maps supported computation graphs to the split form.

contexts.evidence: The 2019 paper documents PyTorch, not Torchvision ImageNet-1K weights or the later ViT-B/16 model. The official Torchvision model documentation does list these checkpoint families. This paper can acknowledge the framework but cannot establish the exact experimental weights.
contexts.proposed_replacement: We use PyTorch~\parencite{Paszke2019PyTorch} with torchvision ImageNet-1K checkpoints~\parencite{Deng2009,Russakovsky2015ilsvrc}\footnote{\url{https://docs.pytorch.org/vision/stable/models.html}}.

notes: No metadata correction is necessary: the supplied author list matches the paper. The official landing page expands Zach to Zachary and drops the Köpf accent, but the PDF supports the existing spelling.

The supplied conference title is an alternate proceedings title for NeurIPS 2019. Exact checkpoint versions and actual converter behavior require the thesis implementation records, not the framework paper.

verified_metadata.title: On the Convergence of the Concave-Convex Procedure
verified_metadata.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 22

metadata_sources.supports: Title page establishes correct author order and initials; full paper verifies the convergence focus.
Official NIPS 2009 proceedings venue and year; its displayed author ordering conflicts with the PDF.
Author institution record agrees with PDF author order and gives pages 1759–1767.

artifact.version_note: Official NIPS 2009 proceedings PDF, 9 pages. PDF author order is Sriperumbudur then Lanckriet, despite reversal in the online metadata/BibTeX.

contexts.evidence: Section 1, Eq. (1), assumes a decomposition f=u−v and analyzes CCCP for optimizing such objectives; Section 3 proves convergence under assumptions. It does not establish DC representability of piecewise-linear functions or neural networks. The citation supports the DC-programming background, but the sentence jointly attributes the existence guarantee to these optimization papers.
contexts.proposed_replacement: Classical \ac{dc} programming~\parencite{Tao1997_DCProgramming,LeThi2018DCA,Sriperumbudur2009CCCP} studies optimization with such decompositions; the representation theory of piecewise-linear functions as differences of convex ones guarantees that the split exists.

notes: Retain the existing author order: it agrees with the actual paper, even though the official proceedings landing page and exported BibTeX reverse it.
The series was branded NIPS in 2009; the supplied NeurIPS parenthesis is modern naming, not a different venue. Optional normalization is Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, volume 22.
